items.title: French lawmakers reportedly add per-gigabyte traffic levy on content platforms to budget
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reports French lawmakers approved an internet levy based on traffic usage, put at about $11.2 billion, charged per gigabyte of content delivered to French subscribers, with US tech firms such as Google and Meta named as targets. A French outlet earlier described a Socialist Party amendment to the 2027 budget at 5.5 centimes per GB. Budget amendments are not law until the full budget passes.
items.why_it_matters: A traffic-volume charge would hit data-heavy streaming and AI-content delivery and revives US-EU digital-tax friction. Net-neutrality objections and a possible US trade response are the next things to watch.

learn.title: Estimate decode throughput from memory bandwidth, then size a fleet
learn.why_today: The CCID item cites 175 trillion daily token calls, a volume you can turn into a rough accelerator count once you know what limits decoding.
learn.explanation: Autoregressive decoding reads every weight once per step, so each step costs about (parameter bytes)/(memory bandwidth) regardless of how many sequences share it. Batching B sequences therefore multiplies throughput by B until compute or KV-cache traffic becomes the bottleneck. Dividing a daily token volume by 86,400 gives tokens per second, and dividing by per-accelerator throughput gives a fleet size. It breaks for long contexts (KV reads grow with length), MoE models (only active experts are read, but batching touches more of them) and speculative decoding. All figures below are illustrative, not any real model or chip.
learn.python:
# Illustrative numbers only: decode is memory-bandwidth bound.
params = 70e9          # parameters
bytes_per = 1          # 8-bit weights
bw = 3.35e12           # bytes/s HBM bandwidth (illustrative accelerator)
batch = 64             # sequences decoded together; weights are read once per step
step_s = params*bytes_per/bw
tok_s = batch/step_s
print(f"step {step_s*1e3:.1f} ms, {tok_s:.0f} tokens/s per accelerator")
target = 175e12/86400  # tokens/s implied by 175T tokens/day
print(f"accelerators for 175T/day at this rate: {target/tok_s:,.0f}")
